:::{#exm-poisson-rate-ratio}
#### Rate ratio for a ten-year age difference

Suppose a Poisson regression model for emergency-room visits
includes age in years, $x_1$,
with coefficient $\b_1 = 0.03$
and no interactions involving age.
By @thm-poisson-rate-ratio with $a = 60$ and $b = 50$,
the rate ratio comparing a 60-year-old to a 50-year-old
with the same values of every other covariate is:

$$
\ba
\rateratio(x_1 = 60 : x_1 = 50)
&= \expf{\b_1 (60 - 50)}
&& \text{(rate ratio theorem)} \\
&= \expf{0.03 \cdot 10}
&& \text{(substitute } \b_1 \text{ and subtract)} \\
&= \expf{0.3}
&& \text{(multiply)} \\
&\approx 1.350
&& \text{(evaluate)}
\ea
$$

A one-year age difference instead gives
$\expf{0.03} \approx 1.030$,
a 3% higher rate per year of age.
The ten-year rate ratio is not ten times the one-year excess:
$\expf{0.3} = \paren{\expf{0.03}}^{10}$,
because rate ratios multiply across successive one-year steps.

:::
